items.title: Exact finite-quotient control of subcritical-density transfer times in ergodic countable abelian actions
items.difficulty_reason: H2: Kneser finite-quotient reduction of a compact difference set alone gives only a model for the compact factor, not equality with the original measurable action transfer set. The author proves the generic-point/action-set correspondence and its overshoot inequality, then uses the positive mass of each finite-quotient atom and the strict density deficit to rule out every missing transfer coset. This recovers an actual factor controlling both sets and the full transfer-time set, under the exact pointwise averaging assumption without a Folner requirement. The full nonroutine correspondence and finite-atom contradiction are supplied.

dedup.scope: Current master exact same-source2044, finite transfer/return-time, Kneser, small-doubling, sumset and factor neighborhoods; no queued batch/current JEP147 material; actual nearest primary statements compared

compared.relation: Same source Theorem1.8 assumes total ergodicity and equality density=sum<1, concluding circle intervals with two endpoint-coset exceptions. New Theorem1.5 has strict subcritical density and an exact finite-quotient transfer set; conditions/conclusion differ, common correspondence core reused.
Actual Theorem1.2 concerns large powers of symmetric open sets in locally compact groups, bounded tripling/approximate groups; no measure-preserving action or exact transfer-time factor.
Actual Theorem1.6 gives a Bohr neighborhood contained in triple commuting finite-index homomorphism sumsets, not exact return-set finite-quotient control.
Actual lemma key is a four-fold covariance estimate under mixing property P, not finite-quotient structure of a transfer-time set.
Actual selected Proposition no reverse implication of main theorems constructs a subset of Z distinguishing density criteria along Folner sequences; not action-set inverse theorem.
Actual theorem main classifies mixed restricted critical sumset pairs in a prime field up to common affine equivalence; not transfer times of an arbitrary ergodic action.
